about: The painted backdrop beyond the outer road's walkable area (map/BUILDING.md: painting, not models). tools/backdrop.mjs restyles each panel from the scroll strip that lies past that edge (scan rect u0,v0,u1,v1) with prompts/backdrop_panel.txt + the panel's content prompt (prompts/backdrop_outer_road_<side>.txt): seen at eye level on plain white, which ship keys out with clean edges; it measures the painted horizon, and web/src/backdrop.js stands the panel on the ring (angles: 0 = east, 90 = north, 180 = west) at its true aspect with that horizon at eye level, its foot in ground mist. Everything outside the painted area is veiled in mist (the scroll's blank silk). West is the gate (S5), built: no panel. North: the silk's top edge cuts the row of buildings and the tree crowns behind the road's north side (the houses and the temple's gate hall at u 9400-10300, pines and willows at 10300-11400 and 11800-12600, the courier post's back hall at 11400-11800); no open ground, field or distance is painted above them, so mist only. South (below the silk's edge): mist only. A panel goes when its neighbouring section is built.

panels.why: the rest of S4 (u 12600-15500: the palm-covered family carts, the crowd round a seated man, the wheelwright, the tea house under the big tree, the moorings with the river leaving the top of the frame) lies past the east seam and is not built yet. The seam leans with the scroll's receding direction, so from the section's centre it spans about -32 to +52 degrees: the panel is centred on 10 and as wide (84), its left (north) end over the moorings
panels.picked: 2026-10-12: candidates 0-1 are the first eye-level draw, 2-3 the second (gen/sections/outer_road/backdrop/draw1_2026-10-12, draw2_2026-10-12). 0 keeps to the strip: the hall with the blue eave cloth and its crowd, the wheelwright, pack donkeys, the huge bare tree over the mat sheds and the tea house, three arched-mat boats on a short reach of water at the road's end, the two palm-hooded carts with oxen, the tiled roofs on the right (it overcounts the donkeys and the tea drinkers). 1 runs the river on as a long canal under a far tree line; 2 moors about ten boats in a row before a far tree line; 3 opens a lake to the horizon
